questions.question: Classify 3x^2 − 5x + 2, x^2 − 9 and 4x^3 by number of terms and degree, giving each its two-word name.
questions.expected_answer: 3x^2 − 5x + 2: three terms, degree 2 — quadratic trinomial. x^2 − 9: two terms, degree 2 — quadratic binomial. 4x^3: one term, degree 3 — cubic monomial (the 3 is the degree, not a count of terms).

questions.question: Simplify 5x − 2x^2 + 3 + 4x^2 − x, write it in standard form, and classify it. Explain why the classification must wait until after simplifying.
questions.expected_answer: Like terms: −2x^2 + 4x^2 = 2x^2; 5x − x = 4x; constant 3. Standard form 2x^2 + 4x + 3: a quadratic trinomial with leading coefficient 2. As written it had five terms, but like terms collapse, so counting before simplifying gives a wrong name — just as 2x + 3x is the monomial 5x, not a binomial.

questions.question: Explain why x/2 is a monomial but 2/x is not a polynomial, and why 3xy is one term rather than three.
questions.expected_answer: x/2 is one half times x — a number dividing, variable exponent 1 — so it is a linear monomial. 2/x is 2 times x^(−1): a negative exponent on the variable, so it is not a polynomial. 3xy is a product of factors 3, x and y with no plus or minus between them; terms are separated only by plus and minus, so it is a single term.
